uncited: The INR Training Loop is the fundamental optimization procedure for fitting an Implicit Neural Representation (INR) to a discrete volumetric dataset.
It solves the problem of learning a continuous function $f_\theta$ that approximates a 3D volume $V$ by minimizing the mean squared error (MSE) between network predictions and ground-truth samples.

It differs from [Neural Surface Rendering Training (Eikonal & Boundary Regularization)](3430-neural-surface-rendering-training-eikonal-boundary-regulariz.md) by focusing on volumetric density/attenuation rather than surface geometry, and from [Global Optimization](5436-global-optimization.md) by using stochastic gradient descent on random batches rather than full-volume or global constraints.
*   Trained network $f_\theta$ representing $V$ as a continuous function.
*   Ground Truth: Scalar $v_j$ obtained via trilinear interpolation.
**Sample:** Uniformly sample $B$ coordinates $\{(x_j, y_j, z_j)\}_{j=1}^B$ from the volume domain.
**Encode:** For each coordinate, compute encoding $e_j \leftarrow \gamma(x_j, y_j, z_j)$.
**Retrieve Ground Truth:** Compute $v_j \leftarrow \text{trilinear}(V, x_j, y_j, z_j)$.
*   **Boundary Conditions:** Trilinear interpolation requires coordinates to be within the volume bounds.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(I \cdot B \cdot C)$, where $I$ is iterations, $B$ is batch size, and $C$ is network evaluation cost.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(N^3)$ for storing $V$ plus $O(C)$ for network parameters.
*   **When to Use:** When a continuous representation is needed for a single volume or when using meta-learning variants.
Originated from standard neural network training practices applied to volumetric data.
